title: agent-atlas Agent manifest
description: A declarative, versioned contract for one agent. OpenAPI in spirit, for agents.

responsibility.description: A single responsibility. If you need the word 'and' to state it, you have two agents.

model.description: Either a single pinned model (the default, reproducible case) OR a reference to a Router for dynamic model selection. Exactly one — never both. An agent is an LLM reasoner; deterministic proving lives in the CONTROLS layer (a gate's pluggable reasoner), never on an agent.

router.description: id of a Router that selects the model dynamically.

input.description: Path to the typed input schema.

output.description: Path to the typed output schema.

tools.description: Allowlist of tool ids this agent may call. An empty list means none.

refusal.description: Refusal is a first-class output: the conditions under which the agent should decline rather than guess.

emits.description: The output value that signals a refusal.

telemetry.description: The decisions this agent records, so 'why did it do that' is answerable.

prohibited_tools.description: NEGATIVE declaration (NIST Govern: 'prohibited actions'). Tool ids this agent must NEVER call, even if otherwise reachable — distinct from the positive `tools` allowlist. Conformance can flag a runtime call to any of these.

grounding_threshold.description: Confidence gate: the agent should refuse rather than answer when grounding/confidence falls below this (e.g. 0.95 for regulated domains). The declared bound conformance checks runtime behavior against.

escalation_to.description: id of the System/Job/queue this agent escalates to on refusal or low confidence — escalation as a named target, not just a refusal flag.

governance.description: Regime-neutral trust/privacy controls (NIST AI RMF: privacy, security, accountability). The control is declared here; which standard it satisfies is named by data_tags and the model-level compliance_regimes. Optional — declare what the requirements state; leave the rest for a human.

data_classification.description: Sensitivity of the data this object touches.

data_tags.description: Regulatory data classes (MULTIPLE may apply, e.g. PHI and PII).

residency.description: Where data may be processed/stored. 'on-prem' = never leaves the boundary.

redaction.description: Fields to filter/redact/drop before telemetry is indexed (so observability isn't a compliance liability).
